frostingGuidance.indoor: Performs beautifully in mild spring temperatures indoors — holds crisp piped detail all day.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Stable in typical spring outdoor temperatures (60-75°F); bring it inside briefly if there's a sudden warm snap before the reception.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Sets smooth and holds sharp lines easily in spring's moderate indoor climate control.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Handles mild spring air well, but watch for spring showers — humidity above roughly 70% can cause the surface to sweat or soften.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Fine indoors if kept away from direct sun through windows; refrigerate until just before serving.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Workable for a short outdoor spring reception but keep it shaded and served within an hour or two of setup.

frostingGuidance.indoor: The safest indoor choice for summer — air conditioning keeps it firm through a full reception.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Can soften above roughly 80°F; keep the cake shaded, avoid direct sun, and consider a brief chill before display.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Holds its shape well in air-conditioned summer venues.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Can weep or develop a sticky sheen in summer heat and humidity above roughly 75°F — minimize display time and keep it out of direct sun.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Only safe with reliable air conditioning; still serve chilled and don't let it sit out long.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: High risk — whipped cream will weep and slump above roughly 75°F, so swap to Swiss meringue buttercream or fondant for an outdoor summer wedding.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Ideal indoor conditions — fall's mild temperatures keep it stable with no extra precautions.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Handles cool fall air well; watch for wind exposure drying the surface during a long outdoor cocktail hour.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Sets and holds detail beautifully in fall's naturally moderate indoor climate.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: One of the best seasons for outdoor fondant — cool, dry fall air is close to ideal working conditions.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Stable and easy to serve indoors once temperatures drop below room-warm.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Fall's cooler air is much friendlier to whipped cream than summer, though a sudden warm afternoon can still soften it — keep it shaded just in case.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Very stable indoors in winter, though a well-heated venue can soften it slightly near heat vents — keep it away from direct airflow.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Cold winter air keeps it firm, but below-freezing temperatures can cause condensation once it's brought back inside — let it temper gradually.

frostingGuidance.indoor: Performs well indoors; low winter humidity is actually ideal for a crisp, dry finish.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Extreme cold can make fondant brittle and prone to cracking — keep transport time short and avoid flexing the cake board in freezing air.

frostingGuidance.indoor: The easiest season for whipped cream indoors — cool ambient temperatures help it hold its shape far longer than summer.
frostingGuidance.outdoor: Cold weather is actually excellent for whipped cream stability, as long as it stays above freezing; below 32°F it can weep once it warms back up for serving.
